prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
For months, the question around the Strait of Hormuz was simple: can ships still pass?

Now, the harder question is this: can either side keep the pressure going?

The United States and Israel began air attacks on Iran on February 28. A ceasefire understanding in June briefly eased the blockade. But after Iran attacked three merchant ships outside routes approved by the United States, the blockade returned on July 14.

Since then, the conflict has not moved toward a clear finish. The United States has kept economic pressure on Iran. Iran has continued to challenge control of the strait. Talks have not produced a new agreement.

On August 18, President Trump said that no talks with Iran were planned. The 60-day period for talks also ended without an agreement. A private political-risk company moved its expected easing of tensions from September to the end of the year.

This is why the conflict now looks less like a short battle and more like a long economic test. Reports point to damage inside Iran, danger around the shipping route, and a continuing diplomatic deadlock.

One report said that a month of relative calm was ending and that the region was moving back toward a dangerous military stalemate that may be hard to sustain.

But the picture is not simple. On September 2, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said that more than 17 million barrels of oil passed through Hormuz on August 31. He called it a wartime record and said Iran was losing its ability to disrupt the strait.

That claim points in one direction. Other evidence points in another.

【Point One】
Wright’s 17 million barrels was a one-day government figure. An energy agency’s 4.9 million barrels was an average for the second quarter. One tanker tracker estimated about 9.1 million barrels for August 31, using a wider sea area. The figures do not measure exactly the same thing. One day cannot prove a lasting recovery.

【Point Two】
The United States says it cleared the main shipping route, but official figures do not give a number. One report said more than 200 mine-like objects were removed, while only 11 were confirmed as mines. The route was still rated “SEVERE.” An Iranian opposition media outlet also reported a petrochemical shutdown and a loss of about 230 million cubic meters of daily gas capacity. Traffic can rise briefly while danger and damage remain.

point_one.reasoning: 政府発表、エネルギー機関、タンカー追跡の数値を具体的に比較し、同じ対象を測っていないため17百万バレルという一日の記録だけでは航路の持続的回復を証明できないと示している。単なる留保ではなく、Full Storyの曖昧な「証拠が分かれる」という点を数値と測定方法の違いで具体化している。

point_two.reasoning: 航路の危険度、除去された物体と確認済み機雷の数、さらにイランのガス供給能力の損失を示し、船舶通航の一時的増加が安全回復や被害解消を意味しないと説明している。Full Storyにあった危険・損害という概略を、具体的な数字とインフラへの影響に掘り下げており、Point Oneの統計比較とも重ならない。
